name: Cupric autonomous video production playbook
purpose: A Cupric-native craft policy distilled from recurring patterns in the attributed Opus 5.5 video case catalogue. It is not model training and does not imply that every case used every rule.
license: MIT for this catalogue/playbook text; third-party references and media retain their own rights.

rules.name: Brief to beat sheet
rules.rule: Turn the brief into a beat sheet before styling: hook in the first second, distinct beats, readable holds, one payoff, and a clean final frame.

rules.name: Single clock render
rules.rule: Use one shared timeline clock for every visual, caption, audio cue, camera move and transition. Preview and export must sample the same pure frame function.

rules.name: Code-first editable motion
rules.rule: Prefer editable native primitives, HTML canvas scenes, Remotion-style compositions, or deterministic SVG/CSS motion over flattened screenshots. Never depend on Date.now, Math.random, CSS animation time, or an external renderer.

rules.name: Hook and pacing
rules.rule: Make the first frame legible and high-contrast, establish the visual grammar quickly, vary scale and composition across beats, and avoid filling every moment with motion.

rules.name: One visual system
rules.rule: Choose one visual system per video: at most two type families, one accent, one caption treatment, one background family, and a small set of repeated easing and transition recipes.

rules.name: Layered production
rules.rule: Build in layers: background or atmosphere, subject/media, typography, accents, captions, then audio. Keep every layer editable and leave safe areas around faces, products and titles.

rules.name: Audio as structure
rules.rule: Treat music, narration and sound effects as timing structure: mark beats, duck music under speech, land key reveals on changes, and keep audio optional when no local source exists.

rules.name: Iterative review passes
rules.rule: Use staged passes instead of one opaque generation: composition pass, motion pass, typography and caption pass, audio pass, then an export QA pass for overflow, contrast, timing, missing media and even dimensions.

rules.name: Safe multi-tool adapters
rules.rule: When a brief calls for a 3D, particle, shader, character or UI treatment, translate the intent into a Cupric-native component or sandboxed source scene. Do not execute arbitrary MCP, After Effects, Blender or remote code inside the desktop app.

rules.name: Real copy and data
rules.rule: Use the user brief, imported media and verified values. Never fabricate testimonials, statistics, reviews, before/after claims, credits or source ownership to make a case study look finished.

rules.name: Social reframe
rules.rule: Design the hero for the requested aspect ratio, then reframe with safe title/action areas. Keep text on the short-side safe zone and create separate queued variants rather than squeezing one composition.

rules.name: Deliverable check
rules.rule: Before declaring success, make a playable MP4, preserve the editable project, report any missing provider or media honestly, and show the exact source/credit trail for borrowed references.
